chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Maskan, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, specified the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) with the noblest of moral traits. Hence, test yourselves; if they are in you, then praise Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, and desire towards Him for more of them. Then he mentioned them, the ten: certainty, contentment, patience, thankfulness, satisfaction, good mannerisms, openhandedness, sense of honor, courage and manliness.

key_terms.الْغَيْرَةُ: Sense of honor/Zeal (in a positive sense)

ai.seo_question: What are the ten noble moral traits specified for the Messenger of Allah that believers should test themselves for?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) presents a diagnostic method for spiritual self-assessment by linking personal virtue to the Prophet’s exemplary character. The ten listed traits—ranging from internal states like certainty (*al-Yaqin*) to social virtues like generosity (*al-Sakha*)—are framed not merely as moral ideals but as divine tests, urging believers to seek divine augmentation of these qualities. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *akhlaq* as the tangible manifestation of faith and the primary means of emulating the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.basel-kadem: 4.	We were told by Muhammed bin Ahmad bin Yahya al-‘Attar, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: I was told by my father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammed bin Isa, from Uthman bin Isa, from Abdullah bin Maskan, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq, (a.s.) that he said:

Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, specified the Messenger of Allah (saww) with the noblest of moral traits. Hence, test yourselves; if they are in you, then praise Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, and desire towards Him for more of them. Then he mentioned them, the ten: certainty, contentment, patience, thankfulness, satisfaction, good mannerisms, openhandedness, sense of honor, courage and manliness.
